brand.name: Saint Luis Rey
brand.description: Not on the site at all - confirmed absent from the site's full brand index, not just a slug issue. DISAMBIGUATION: there are two distinct trademarks both called 'Saint Luis Rey.' A Cuban version made by Habanos S.A. (Briones Montoto factory, Havana, Vuelta Abajo tobacco) is a separate, embargoed product not covered here. This entry covers the non-Cuban 'Saint Luis Rey' distributed by Altadis USA, which traces its name to a Cuban brand registered in the 1940s and nationalized by Cuba in 1960. The modern non-Cuban Honduran blend was created in 1996 by Christian Eiroa, originally produced at Tabacos Rancho Jamastran for distributor Max Rohr Imports; production moved to Flor de Copan after Max Rohr was absorbed into what became Altadis. A reformulated 'SLR Gen2' was released in 2013. Positioned as an accessible-premium brand (roughly $6-9/stick retail). Altadis USA's own '1918' marketing tagline refers to the company's founding, not the brand's - not used as the brand's founded date.
brand.founded_note: 1996 is when the modern non-Cuban Honduran blend was created by Christian Eiroa. The Saint Luis Rey name itself traces to a Cuban trademark registered in the 1940s (separate, embargoed Habanos S.A. product today).
brand.origin_country: Honduras (primary manufacturing location for most lines); Dominican Republic (Tabacales line only, since 2025 - does not share the brand's default Honduran origin)

line.name: Saint Luis Rey Carenas
line.description: Named for Puerto de Carenas, the old name for Havana harbor. Medium-bodied, earthy spice and salty notes, oily Nicaraguan wrapper over an aged Honduran core.
line.factory: Flor de Copan, Santa Rosa de Copan, Honduras
